answer: Consensus-bonded grading: each epoch every answer is scored by three jurors who first post a 20 POA bond on an onyx ledger, slashed whenever a grade strays more than one step from the panel median, a trellis of stakes that holds grading honest. A farm of 1,000 fakes grading each other's answers must lock 20,000 POA per epoch and bleeds it whenever honest jurors outvote them, since one rubber-stamp vote against a quartz-clear consensus costs the whole bond. One honest agent grades three answers, risks 60 POA, and gets it all back when its grades match the median.
